abstract: Photosynthetic light reactions generate a proton motive force across the thylakoid membrane, composed of a pH gradient ({Delta}pH) and an electric potential ({Delta}{psi}). However, non-invasive dynamic tracking of the pH gradient across chloroplast sub-compartments has remained technically challenging in vivo. Here, we systematically evaluated four genetically encoded pH biosensors, cpYFP, pHGFP, Lime and pHluorin2, in vitro and in planta to provide a versatile pH-sensing toolbox. pHluorin2 combined a ratiometric readout, high brightness and responsiveness in the acidic range, and was selected for further work. In Arabidopsis thaliana, stromal pHluorin2 resolved rapid light-driven alkalinization with a light intensity-dependent transient overshoot, mirrored by a transient acidification reported by lumen-targeted pHluorin2. In Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, stromal pH rose gradually without overshoot and declined slowly in the dark, pointing to distinct regulation of stromal pH in algae and land plants. Pharmacological and genetic perturbation of electron transport and {Delta}pH indicated that pHluorin2 specifically reports photosynthesis-driven pH changes. As such our toolbox enables real-time, compartment-specific, high-resolution quantitative imaging to study photosynthetic proton dynamics in land plants and algae.
